findings.title: Stale `Strategy::C` terminology locked into the public ErrorCode + EngineError variant name + observable error message string across 3 cross-language surfaces — freeze-time wire-locks the obsolete name forever post-`v1-beta`
findings.description: Strategy::C was renamed to Strategy::Reserved at G23-0a per arch-r1-14 (closing CRATES-DEEP-DIVE §4 named-but-deferred item); the variant lives at `crates/benten-ivm/src/strategy.rs:84` as `Reserved`. But the cross-language error mirror still encodes the obsolete `C` name across THREE surfaces that V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE item 4 (D2 v1-canonical-bytes) + item 10 (TS/JS public API) locks bytewise: (a) Rust variant `EngineError::ViewStrategyCReserved` at `crates/benten-engine/src/error.rs:119` with format-string `"user view '{view_id}' declared Strategy::C — Strategy C (Z-set / DBSP cancellation) is reserved for Phase 3+"` (the Rust variant FIRES from engine_views.rs:696 when caller supplied Strategy::Reserved — internal-inconsistency hazard at runtime), (b) `ErrorCode::ViewStrategyCReserved` + stable wire string `"E_VIEW_STRATEGY_C_RESERVED"` at `crates/benten-errors/src/lib.rs:334 + 1536 + 2367` (3 sites), (c) TS class `EViewStrategyCReserved` + wire code `E_VIEW_STRATEGY_C_RESERVED` at `packages/engine/src/errors.generated.ts:1320 + 3225` whose docstring at line 1318 says "declared Strategy::Reserved" — INCONSISTENT with the Rust format-string on the same code-path. Once `v1-beta` tags, the wire code `E_VIEW_STRATEGY_C_RESERVED` is bytewise-frozen forever (item 4 P-III); renaming post-`v1-GM` would be a SemVer break + a Phase-3+ wire-format break. The error message users see in production will permanently reference an enum variant name (`Strategy::C`) that does NOT exist in any Rust source.

findings.title: `Engine::walk_share_scope` is principal-unbearing at v1-beta; the principal-bearing `walk_share_scope_as` is named ADDITIVE Composing-time enhancement at engine_share_scope.rs:46-49 but the lack of an `_as` overload at v1-beta means EVERY consumer using walk_share_scope at v1-beta loses the per-principal recipient enumeration the BFS-order canonical-path contract assumes for path-tagged-key derivation (RATIFIED-S&C §R4 + 15(h)).
findings.description: Engine::walk_share_scope per V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE item 15(h) is the v1-beta public consumer surface; its signature `(&self, &Spec) -> Result<WalkResult, EngineError>` does NOT carry a principal arg. The doc at engine_share_scope.rs:46-49 explicitly notes 'principal-bearing variants (e.g. walk_share_scope_as(&self, principal, spec)) are ADDITIVE Composing-time enhancements that may co-exist.' But the BFS canonical-path contract per RATIFIED-S&C §R4 + item 15(h) states 'recipients walk the same BFS the producer enumerated; canonical path carried in AuthorizationGrant.key_material per (d) + (f)' — this carries an implicit recipient-principal context. At v1-beta with only the non-`_as` variant exposed, every recipient-side walk_share_scope call walks AS the engine's default principal (whatever the call-site Engine handle is bound to), which is a semantic gap relative to the recipient-principal that produced the path-tagged key the recipient is consuming. The cross-walk parity test at g_core_9_walk_share_scope_e2e.rs validates BYTE-equality of the walk's enumeration order; it does NOT validate principal-aware semantics because there is none at v1-beta. This may be intentional (the recipient's local engine has only ONE principal — the recipient — so the implicit binding is correct in practice) — but it's worth surfacing whether the freeze codifies that property explicitly.
evidence: crates/benten-engine/src/engine_share_scope.rs:60 walk_share_scope signature (no principal arg)
crates/benten-engine/src/engine_share_scope.rs:46-49 explicit Composing-time enhancement deferral
RATIFIED-S&C §R4 quoted in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md lines 1520-1528 — recipient-side walk semantics
findings.impact: Possible. If a deployment shape ever runs multi-principal in the same engine handle (e.g. test fixtures, plugin-as-principal sub-walks), the implicit principal binding will be ambiguous post-freeze + un-fixable without an additive `_as` variant. The Composing-time `_as` addition is genuinely additive (does not break the v1-beta surface), so the cost is asymmetric: missing the `_as` at v1-beta is recoverable; having a wrong implicit-principal pinning at v1-beta is also recoverable since the implicit semantic is conservative (default-engine-principal).
findings.disposition_for_freeze_wave: DISAGREE-WITH-EXPLANATION (lens-author's call). The freeze spec correctly defers `_as` to Composing. The v1-beta semantic that ships — implicit binding to the engine's default principal — is the conservative-correct shape for the single-principal recipient case (the common case for shape (a) full peers + shape (c) embedded webview). Multi-principal recipient walks are a Composing-time feature; the additive Composing addition does not break the v1-beta surface. RECOMMEND: surface this in the freeze-spec body as an explicit 'what's NOT frozen at v1-beta' bullet under item 15(h) (one line: 'Principal-bearing walk variants are ADDITIVE Composing-time enhancements; v1-beta walks bind implicitly to the engine handle's default principal'). Closes the disposition without code change.
